rows.experiment_summary: This experiment established the performance floor for the multimodal cellular profiling study using the minimal RNA-only configuration (single profile, PCA-2000 encoder, no image encoder, no aggregation, no fusion), achieving a validation accuracy of 0.485 and F1 of 0.464. As the first completed experiment, this result serves as a baseline reference point; no comparative evidence yet exists to attribute this performance to any specific design choice. It remains uncertain whether more complex RNA encoders (e.g., scvi, scgpt), multiprofile aggregation, image modalities, or multimodal fusion can meaningfully improve upon this ~0.485 accuracy floor.
rows.selection_reason: No experiments have been completed, so there is no evidence for any design choice. The most critical uncertainty is the absolute performance floor: how well does the simplest possible configuration (RNA-only, single-profile, PCA-2000) perform? Establishing this baseline is essential before interpreting whether more complex encoders (scvi, scgpt), multiprofile aggregation (avgpool, transformer), image modalities, or multimodal fusion actually add value. Config_001 is the minimal configuration in the design space—no image encoder, no aggregation, no fusion—making it the cleanest reference point. All subsequent experiments can be understood as adding one or more design choices on top of this floor, which allows us to isolate the marginal contribution of each decision. Under a limited budget, spending one experiment on the simplest baseline maximizes the information gained per experiment by anchoring the entire comparison grid.

rows.experiment_summary: This experiment replaced the PCA-2000 linear encoder with the learned scvi_n200 nonlinear encoder while holding all other design variables constant (single profile, RNA-only, no aggregation, no fusion), yielding a validation accuracy of 0.520 and F1 of 0.498 versus the PCA baseline of 0.485 and 0.464. Because exactly one variable (the RNA encoder) was changed, the ~3.5-point accuracy gain is cleanly attributable to the encoder choice, indicating that nonlinear learned representations provide a modest but real improvement over linear projection in the RNA-only setting. However, absolute performance remains moderate, leaving it uncertain whether the RNA signal itself is the primary bottleneck and whether the scvi encoder's advantage will persist when combined with multiprofile aggregation or image-based multimodal fusion.
rows.selection_reason: Evidence: Only one experiment is complete (config_001: RNA-only, single profile, PCA-2000 → acc 0.485, F1 0.464), establishing a low baseline. The largest source of uncertainty is whether the RNA representation itself is the bottleneck—PCA-2000 is a linear projection, while scvi_n200 is a learned nonlinear latent representation specifically designed for single-cell data. Question: Does replacing the linear PCA encoder with the learned scvi encoder (holding profile setting, modality, aggregation, and fusion all identical to the baseline) meaningfully improve validation accuracy? Why this is the best next experiment: It changes exactly one design variable (RNA encoder) relative to the established baseline, making the comparison clean and interpretable. If scvi substantially outperforms PCA, it confirms that representation quality is a primary lever and justifies further investment in encoder choice and downstream multimodal designs built on scvi. If it does not, it signals that the RNA signal alone is limited, redirecting budget toward image or multimodal experiments. Under a tight budget, isolating the encoder effect before layering on multiprofile aggregation or image fusion avoids confounding multiple changes and yields the highest information-per-experiment.

rows.experiment_summary: This experiment established the performance floor for the image modality using a single-profile, image-only configuration with a ResNet-50 encoder (no RNA, no aggregation, no fusion), achieving a validation accuracy of 0.208 and F1 of 0.172. This is substantially below the RNA-only baselines (0.485 for PCA-2000, 0.520 for scvi_n200), suggesting that image features carry very weak independent predictive signal for this classification task. It remains uncertain whether image features could still contribute meaningfully when fused with RNA representations, whether alternative image encoders or preprocessing might recover more signal, or whether the low performance reflects a fundamental limitation of the image modality for this task.
rows.selection_reason: 1) Evidence/uncertainty: We have two RNA-only single-profile experiments showing that a learned nonlinear encoder (scvi_n200, 0.520 acc) modestly beats a linear one (PCA-2000, 0.485 acc). However, the image modality is entirely unexplored—we have zero data on whether image features carry independent predictive signal. This is the largest source of uncertainty in the design space, as it determines whether the 36 multimodal configurations (configs 016-051) are worth pursuing at all. 2) What this tests: config_010 (image-only, single profile, ResNet-50) establishes the performance floor for the image modality in direct analogy to how config_001 established the RNA floor. It isolates the image encoder's contribution with no confounding from RNA, aggregation, or fusion. 3) Why it is the best next experiment: Before investing limited budget in complex multimodal fusion or multiprofile aggregation, we need to know whether the image signal is strong enough to be worth combining. If image-only performs competitively (≥0.50), multimodal fusion becomes a high-priority direction; if it is weak (<0.45), we should focus remaining budget on RNA improvements (multiprofile, scgpt encoder). This single experiment gates the entire multimodal branch of the search and is the highest-information, lowest-confounding next step.

rows.experiment_summary: This experiment tested multiprofile aggregation (avgpool) on the scvi_n200 RNA encoder, changing only the profile/aggregation axis from the best prior RNA-only result (single-profile scvi_n200, 0.520 acc / 0.498 F1), and achieved a validation accuracy of 0.650 and F1 of 0.628. Because the encoder and modality were held constant, the ~13-point accuracy gain is cleanly attributable to the multiprofile + avgpool aggregation, confirming that combining multiple profiles adds substantial predictive signal beyond what the single-profile scvi_n200 representation captures. It remains uncertain whether more expressive aggregation strategies (e.g., transformer) could yield further gains, whether this multiprofile advantage persists once an image modality is introduced, and how much additional headroom exists above the current ~0.65 accuracy.
rows.selection_reason: Evidence: scvi_n200 outperforms PCA-2000 by ~3.5 points in the single-profile RNA-only setting (0.520 vs 0.485), establishing scvi_n200 as the best RNA encoder so far. Image-only resnet50 is very weak (0.208), suggesting the RNA pipeline should be optimized before adding a multimodal component. Uncertainty: it is unknown whether multiprofile aggregation adds meaningful signal on top of the scvi_n200 encoder, or whether the single-profile representation already captures the relevant information. This experiment (config_005: scvi_n200, multiprofile, avgpool) tests exactly that question with the simplest aggregation strategy, changing only the profile/aggregation axis from the best RNA-only result (config_004). If avgpool yields a clear gain, it justifies testing transformer aggregation next; if it does not, it suggests multiprofile is not a productive direction and budget should shift to encoder comparison (scgpt) or multimodal fusion. This is the highest-information-per-experiment choice because it resolves a key design axis (profile aggregation) on the strongest known RNA backbone before committing budget to more complex multimodal or aggregation variants.

rows.experiment_summary: This experiment replaced avgpool with transformer aggregation in the multiprofile scvi_n200 RNA-only setting (the single-variable change from the current best, config_005), achieving a validation accuracy of 0.653 and F1 of 0.628 versus 0.650 and 0.628 for avgpool. The negligible ~0.3-point accuracy difference suggests that a more expressive transformer aggregation provides no meaningful improvement over simple average pooling for combining multi-profile scvi_n200 representations, indicating the aggregation axis is near its practical ceiling under the current encoder. It remains uncertain whether this null result generalizes to other encoders (e.g., scgpt) or whether the remaining headroom lies in the encoder-choice axis or the multimodal fusion question, which are the next unexplored design axes.
rows.selection_reason: The strongest finding so far is that multiprofile aggregation (avgpool) on scvi_n200 RNA yielded a ~13-point accuracy gain (0.520→0.650, config_005), making aggregation the most impactful design axis identified. The key uncertainty is whether avgpool is near-optimal or whether a more expressive transformer aggregation can extract additional signal from the multi-profile representations. config_006 changes exactly one variable (aggregation: avgpool→transformer) relative to the current best (config_005), cleanly isolating the aggregation effect. If transformer outperforms avgpool, it reveals further headroom in the aggregation axis and justifies exploring transformer in multimodal settings later; if it does not, it confirms avgpool is sufficient and redirects the budget toward other axes (encoder choice via scgpt, or the multimodal fusion question). This is the highest-information next step because it directly extends the largest observed effect with a minimal, interpretable change, avoiding the confound of simultaneously introducing a weak image modality (config_010 showed image alone is only 0.208) before fully characterizing the RNA-side design space.

rows.experiment_summary: This experiment swapped the RNA encoder from scvi_n200 to scgpt while holding the multiprofile + avgpool RNA-only configuration constant (the single-variable change from the current best, config_004), achieving a validation accuracy of 0.530 and F1 of 0.515 versus 0.650 and 0.628 for scvi_n200 in the identical multiprofile avgpool setting. Because only the encoder was changed, the ~12-point accuracy drop is cleanly attributable to the encoder choice, indicating that scvi_n200 is the substantially superior RNA encoder for this classification task and that the ~0.65 accuracy ceiling observed with scvi_n200 is not an artifact of the encoder. It remains uncertain whether scgpt could perform differently under alternative aggregation strategies or in a multimodal fusion context, and whether the remaining headroom above 0.65 lies in the fusion axis or in further tuning of the scvi_n200 pipeline.
rows.selection_reason: Evidence: The current best (config_005/006, ~0.65 acc) uses scvi_n200 with multiprofile avgpool. We've cleanly isolated that multiprofile aggregation contributes +13pp over single-profile and that transformer vs avgpool is negligible. The one major RNA encoder axis still untested is scgpt. Question: Does scgpt outperform scvi_n200 in the multiprofile setting, i.e., can we push beyond the ~0.65 ceiling by swapping the encoder while holding the proven-best profile/aggregation settings constant? Why this is the best next experiment: config_008 (scgpt, multiprofile, avgpool) changes exactly one variable (RNA encoder) relative to config_005, giving a clean encoder comparison in the highest-performing regime. It avoids the very-weak image modality (0.208 acc) where fusion gains are unlikely, and it avoids redundant aggregation variants (transformer ≈ avgpool). If scgpt matches or beats scvi, it informs which encoder to pair with multimodal fusion later; if it underperforms, it confirms scvi_n200 as the best encoder and redirects budget toward the fusion axis.

rows.experiment_summary: This experiment tested the first multimodal configuration by adding ResNet50 image features with simple concat fusion to the proven best RNA pipeline (scvi_n200, multiprofile, avgpool), achieving a validation accuracy of 0.632 and F1 of 0.607. This is slightly below the RNA-only best (0.650 acc / 0.628 F1), indicating that the addition of ResNet50 image features via concat fusion does not provide incremental predictive value over the strong RNA representation and may introduce a small amount of noise. It remains uncertain whether alternative fusion strategies (e.g., weighted or attention-based) or different image encoders (e.g., ViT) could extract complementary signal from the image modality, or whether the image features are fundamentally uninformative for this classification task.
rows.selection_reason: The RNA-only pipeline is now well-characterized: scvi_n200 is the clear best encoder (config_004 vs 001, config_008), multiprofile+avgpool gives the largest single gain (+13pp, config_005), and transformer aggregation adds nothing over avgpool (config_006). The current best is ~0.65 accuracy. The biggest remaining uncertainty is the multimodal fusion axis, which is completely untested. Image alone (ResNet50, config_010) is very weak (0.208), so it is genuinely uncertain whether image features add complementary signal or merely noise when fused with the strong RNA representation. Config_030 takes the proven best RNA pipeline (scvi_n200, multiprofile, avgpool) and adds ResNet50 image features with the simplest possible fusion (concat), changing only the modality/fusion axis. This directly answers whether the image modality contributes any incremental value above the 0.65 RNA-only ceiling. If concat helps, weighted fusion and ViT encoders become natural follow-ups; if it does not, we avoid wasting budget on the full 24-config multimodal grid. This is the highest-information experiment under the remaining budget because it resolves the single largest open design question with a minimal, interpretable change.

rows.experiment_summary: This experiment changed only the fusion strategy from concat to weighted in the multimodal setting (scvi_n200, multiprofile, avgpool, ResNet50), achieving a validation accuracy of 0.678 and F1 of 0.646, a ~4.6-point improvement over the identical pipeline with concat fusion (0.632 acc / 0.607 F1) and ~2.8 points above the RNA-only best (0.650 acc / 0.628 F1). Because the single-variable change isolates the fusion axis, the gain is attributable to weighted fusion, indicating that ResNet50 image features carry complementary predictive signal that simple concatenation was suppressing and that proper modality weighting is necessary to unlock it. This resolves the key uncertainty from the prior concat experiment: the image modality is worth pursuing, justifying further investment in stronger image encoders (e.g., ViT-L) and alternative fusion strategies. It remains uncertain whether the weighted-fusion advantage generalizes to other image encoders, whether additional headroom exists above 0.678, and whether more sophisticated fusion mechanisms (e.g., attention-based) could yield further gains.
rows.selection_reason: Evidence: config_030 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, ResNet50, avgpool, concat) achieved 0.632 acc, slightly below the RNA-only best (0.650/0.653), suggesting concat fusion of weak image features introduces noise. However, it remains unclear whether the image modality is fundamentally uninformative or whether the simple concat fusion is the bottleneck. Question: config_031 changes only the fusion strategy from concat to weighted, holding all other variables constant (scvi_n200, multiprofile, avgpool, ResNet50). This isolates the fusion axis. If weighted fusion recovers performance toward or above 0.650, it indicates the image carries complementary signal that needs proper weighting, justifying further investment in image encoders (e.g., ViT-L). If it does not help, it strongly suggests ResNet50 image features are uninformative for this task, allowing us to deprioritize the image modality and focus budget on other axes. This is the most informative single-variable experiment because it directly resolves the key uncertainty about whether the image modality is worth pursuing, and the result will guide all subsequent multimodal decisions.

rows.experiment_summary: This experiment replaced the ResNet50 image encoder with an ImageNet-pretrained ViT-L (imagenet_vit_l) while holding all other settings constant (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, avgpool, weighted fusion), achieving a validation accuracy of 0.706 and F1 of 0.667, a ~2.8-point accuracy improvement over the identical pipeline with ResNet50 (0.678 acc / 0.646 F1). Because only the image encoder was changed, the gain is cleanly attributable to the encoder, confirming that a stronger, more expressive visual representation extracts meaningfully more complementary signal beyond what ResNet50 captures and further justifying continued investment in the image modality. It remains uncertain whether the ~0.706 accuracy approaches a practical ceiling for this task, whether alternative fusion strategies (e.g., attention-based) could yield further gains, or whether even stronger image encoders would continue to produce incremental improvements.
rows.selection_reason: The current best (config_031: multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, resnet50, avgpool, weighted; 0.678 acc) shows that image features do carry complementary signal when properly fused, but ResNet50's standalone performance was very weak (0.208). The key remaining uncertainty is whether a stronger, more expressive image encoder (ImageNet-pretrained ViT-L) can extract meaningfully more complementary visual signal beyond what ResNet50 captures. Config_037 changes exactly one variable (image encoder: resnet50 → imagenet_vit_l) while holding the proven optimal settings constant (scvi_n200, multiprofile, avgpool, weighted fusion), making the result cleanly attributable to encoder quality. This is the highest-value next experiment because: (1) the fusion axis is confirmed productive (weighted >> concat), so a better image representation should yield larger gains; (2) the aggregation axis is near-ceiling (avgpool ≈ transformer), so no need to revisit it; (3) the RNA encoder is settled (scvi_n200 >> scgpt); and (4) this directly tests whether further investment in the image modality is justified or whether the ~0.678 level is near the practical ceiling for this task.

rows.experiment_summary: This experiment replaced avgpool with transformer aggregation in the current best multimodal pipeline (scvi_n200, multiprofile, imagenet_vit_l, weighted fusion), a single-variable change from config_037, achieving a validation accuracy of 0.725 and F1 of 0.685, a ~1.9-point accuracy and ~1.8-point F1 improvement over the avgpool baseline (0.706 acc / 0.667 F1). This contrasts with the near-null result (~0.3 pts) observed for the same aggregation swap in the RNA-only setting, suggesting that transformer aggregation extracts profile-level structure that is specifically beneficial when the RNA representation is subsequently fused with image features via weighted fusion, though the mechanism behind this interaction remains unverified. It is uncertain whether the ~1.9-point gain is robust across random seeds, whether further headroom exists above 0.725 from other unexplored axes (e.g., attention-based fusion, alternative encoder combinations), and whether the aggregation–fusion interaction generalizes beyond the current configuration.
rows.selection_reason: The current best is config_037 (scvi_n200, multiprofile, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted) at 0.706 acc / 0.667 F1. The aggregation axis showed a near-null result in the RNA-only setting (avgpool 0.650 vs transformer 0.653, ~0.3 pts), but that null was measured without an image modality. In the multimodal pipeline, the aggregated RNA representation is subsequently fused with image features via weighted fusion, so the interaction between aggregation strategy and downstream fusion may differ. Config_039 is a single-variable change from config_037 (avgpool → transformer, all else identical), cleanly isolating whether transformer aggregation extracts additional profile-level structure that benefits the weighted fusion step. If it yields a meaningful gain, it identifies a new lever above 0.706; if it is again null, it confirms the aggregation axis is saturated in the multimodal context and redirects remaining budget toward other unexplored axes. This is the most efficient exploitation of the current best direction while resolving the last untested design variable in the proven pipeline.
